title: SLO‑Surgery: Rapid Stabilization & Rollback Orchestration for Multi‑Mode Model Regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
A high-severity customer escalation surfaced a coherent class of generation regressions during an automated canary rollout for model v2.3. The failures appear in hosted and dedicated deployments and intermittently in private installs with older KV cache versions. Impact: elevated error_rate, repeated safety filter hits, and token output truncation for long-context requests. This ticket codifies a fast stabilization playbook (SLO‑Surgery): triage signals, containment actions across deployment modes, automated rollback orchestration, and short-term customer communications.

Scope and goals:
- Contain customer-visible regressions within 30 minutes of pager alert.
- Restore baseline SLOs (latency and quality) within 2 hours or initiate cross-env rollback.
- Provide clear customer-facing comms for hosted, and runbook snippets for Dedicated/Private customers on mitigation and expected timelines.
- Produce one hotpatch PR for runtime if kernel/quantization bug identified; otherwise coordinate model pin + KV cache reconciliation.

Signals and triage checklist (ordered):
1) Observability triggers: generation_failure_rate > 5% over 5m, safety_filter_rate delta > 2x baseline, 95p latency regression, and spike in perplexity monitor on eval prompts.
2) Cross-check model catalog: confirm model binary hash matches release artifact and verify quantization profile used in the rollout.
3) Correlate with autoscaler and serving logs for OOMs, kernel fallback traces, and stale KV cache warnings.
4) Reproduce on a dedicated small cluster with same hardware/kernel flags using the failing prompt set (run eval harness).

Containment play (first 30–90 minutes):
- Immediate: Pause rollout in controller and flip rollout mode to manual freeze for all slices. Record freeze event with metadata for audit.
- Traffic routing: For Hosted, divert traffic for impacted customers to model v2.2 (pinned) via route override. For Dedicated, push a routing override to per-tenant routing table; for Private, provide the exact CLI snippet + patch to apply.
- Short‑circuiting: Enable circuit-breaker threshold for request lengths > configured safe_window to avoid token truncation cascades.
- KV cache: If cache version mismatch suspected, issue a staged cache invalidation for affected routing buckets (see KV‑Invalidate script reference).
- Observability: Turn on verbose generation tracing for a small fraction (1%) of requests and persist full traces for forensic analysis.

Rollback orchestration design decisions:
- Prefer model-level pinning (fastest) for hosted/dedicated; only perform binary rollback for private deployments when model pinning is not supported.
- When rollback is chosen, apply it as an atomic route switch with a 1-minute grace for draining in-flight KV state. The controller will annotate the rollback with incident id and changelog link.
- Maintain a warm pool of last-known-good variant on each pod to reduce cold-start oscillation during rollbacks.
- If a kernel or quantization regression is detected, trigger a limited hotpatch rollout to the runtime (runtime-1.21.patch1) alongside model pinning to reduce customer impact.

Operational playbook (step-by-step):
1) Pager -> Triage owner (oncall eng) acknowledges and tags "SLO‑Surgery".
2) Run quick reproducer: use failing prompt set against canary slice in sandbox cluster. Capture seed, config, and model hash.
3) Decision gate: If reproduces and quality delta > configured threshold -> initiate containment routing and prepare rollback PR.
4) Notify PM and Customer Success; draft hosted bulletin and Dedicated/Private mitigation notes.
5) Execute rollback: controller applies route override, waits for drain_interval (60s), then verifies traffic metrics for 5m.
6) If rollback fails to restore SLOs, escalate to cross-team incident bridge with infra and runtime leads.
7) Post‑incident: run full regression suite, root cause analysis, and propose either hotpatch or model artifact re-release.

Private/Dedicated specific guidance:
- Private: provide signed CLI patch + migration plan. If customer unable to apply within SLA window, offer temporary hosted reroute (where contractual).
- Dedicated: coordinate with account engineering to apply routing override via tenant admin API; confirm disk-backed KV cache consistency.

Customer communication templates (short):
- Hosted bulletin: "We detected a model regression affecting some requests and have temporarily reverted traffic for your workloads to a known stable model. We are investigating and will follow up within 2 hours with next steps."
- Dedicated/Private: "A regression was observed during an automated rollout. We recommend applying the attached routing override to pin to the previous model. Our on-call will assist or provide a signed patch."

Engineering artifacts and links:
- Incident dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/ENG-142089 (internal)
- Reproducer harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/regression-harness/tree/ENG-142089
- Candidate hotpatch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2987
- KV invalidation tool: gs://redwood-tools/kvcache/invalidate_v2.sh

Open design trade-offs noted:
- Preferring model pinning reduces blast radius but can mask runtime regressions; we explicitly log both the model and runtime snapshot at freeze time.
- Aggressive cache invalidation reduces stale-state regressions but increases cold-start cost; we adopt a staged invalidation by routing bucket.

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket):
- A tested, documented SLO‑Surgery runbook merged to docs/operational/slo-surgery.md.
- Automated controller change that supports atomic route switches annotated with incident metadata (controller PR merged).
- One validated hotpatch or model-pinning flow proved on sandbox cluster and rolled out to production as required.

Follow-ups / next steps after incident stabilization:
- Create a durable monitor for model-release-to-quality-delta and add to Pager thresholds.
- Expand reproducer prompt set to include high-risk customer prompts seen in this incident.
- Postmortem with timeline + corrective engineering tasks assigned to owners.
